title: India-Origin UK Mayors Say Public Sentiment on Immigration Has Changed
excerpt: Tushar Kumar, Britain's youngest Indian-origin mayor, and his mother Parveen Rani, Hertsmere's first Indian-origin mayor, addressed the NDTV World Summit session 'From Rohtak to Mayors in the UK.'
body:
• India-origin mayors Tushar Kumar and Parveen Rani told NDTV at the NDTV World Summit 2026 in New Delhi that public sentiment on immigration has changed, in a session titled "The Diaspora Impact: From Rohtak to Mayors in the UK."
  • Kumar, 23, is the youngest Indian-origin mayor in the UK, leading Elstree and Borehamwood Town Council in Hertfordshire; his mother Parveen Rani is the first Indian-origin mayor of Hertsmere Borough Council.
  • The family moved from Rohtak, Haryana, to Britain in 2013, when Kumar was 10. He was elected a councillor at 20 while studying at King's College London.
  • Kumar has said racist abuse on social media is becoming more common, a concrete sign for diaspora families of the harder climate the mayors described.

Two India-origin mayors from Britain — a mother and son who moved from Rohtak to Hertfordshire 13 years ago — told NDTV that public sentiment on immigration has changed, speaking at the NDTV World Summit 2026 in New Delhi on October 22-23. Their session, "The Diaspora Impact: From Rohtak to Mayors in the UK," put two serving mayors who arrived in Britain as immigrants on a summit stage otherwise dominated by ministers, central bankers and diplomats.

Tushar Kumar, 23, is mayor of Elstree and Borehamwood Town Council and the youngest Indian-origin mayor in the United Kingdom. His mother, Parveen Rani, is mayor of Hertsmere Borough Council, the first person of Indian origin to hold that post. The two were elected a week apart in May: Kumar on May 13 and Rani on May 20, according to PTI reporting carried by Devdiscourse.

From Rohtak to Hertfordshire

The family traces its roots to Rohna village in Haryana's Sonipat district and lived in Rohtak before moving to the UK in 2013. "We had not come with any specific thing in mind when we moved to the UK in 2013. Tushar was just 10 years then," his father, businessman Sunil Dahiya, told PTI. The family began with social and charity work, with no political background, and both mother and son were first elected as councillors in 2023.

Kumar attended Loxford School in Ilford and studied political science at King's College London, according to a profile in The Times of India. He contested seats on both Hertsmere Borough Council and Elstree and Borehamwood Town Council while still a student, missed the borough seat, and won the town council seat after a recount as a Labour member. He later served as deputy mayor before becoming mayor. Rani previously served as Hertsmere's cabinet member for Streetscene, Parks, Leisure and Culture and as deputy mayor.

"Today, it is a matter of great pride that a mother and her son from a family who are of Indian origin have become mayors at the same time."

— Sunil Dahiya, the mayors' husband and father, to PTI

A Harder Climate for Immigrants

The mayors' warning to NDTV lands against a record Kumar has described before. He says he is proud of both his British and Indian identities and states plainly that Britain is his home. That sense of belonging has not insulated him from hostility: he has reported receiving racist comments on Facebook and Instagram, and believes such abuse is becoming more common, with some people now feeling more at ease expressing prejudice online, The Times of India reported.

The family's work has also been practical rather than symbolic. Both mayors have taught Hindi free of cost to children born and brought up in the UK, and Kumar is connected with the Hindi Shiksha Parishad, a charity-based organisation, PTI reported. Kumar has said his decision to enter public life was shaped by watching his mother's community work at close hand.

What It Means for the Diaspora

Their route offers a usable map for Indian families abroad: enter through volunteering and local charity work, contest a council seat — Kumar did so at 20, while an undergraduate — and treat the town or borough council, not Parliament, as the first rung. In Hertfordshire, that path produced two mayors in one household within 13 years of arrival.

What's Next

Both mayors are serving their terms in Hertfordshire while carrying the summit's diaspora message back to Britain. Kumar has said that when his year in office ends he intends to aim high, naming the office of Prime Minister as his long-term goal. For now, their test is the one they named in New Delhi: whether local leaders who are themselves immigrants can shift a public conversation on immigration that they say has already changed.
